feature: Tilt, flip and push layers in depth from the canvas and the panel
summary: A picked layer can now be swung and tipped in 3D by two arcs that grow out of its turn knob, pushed back by a blue arrow off its middle, typed exactly in a new 3D section of the panel (keyable), and seen through a camera you set on the frame. Layer and right-click menus have Reset 3D Rotation, Bring Nearer and Send Further; View has Show Camera Settings and Reset Camera.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording (or any recording) and type a title on it with the Text tool.

try.do: Pick the title with V and rest the pointer on the round turn knob above it: a green arc and a red arc appear.
Drag the green arc to the right about two finger widths: the title swings, the pill under it says Rotation Y, and the 3D section in the panel follows.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the diamond on the 3D section's Rotation Y row, step a second forward, and drag the green arc further right until it reads 180: the title now flips over that second.
Scrub back through that second and watch the flip.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the blue arrow off the title's middle upward to push it away; try Option Command [ and ] too.
Draw a rectangle, drag its knob itself (not an arc) and move it: it turns flat exactly as before and its 3D rows stay 0.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Choose View, Show Camera Settings, type 300 into Camera depth, then choose View, Reset Camera.

evaluate: Did you find the arcs on your own by resting on the knob, or did you need to be told they were there?
Is 0.6 degrees per point the right speed for the arcs, or does a flip need too long a drag?
Is the green arc for Rotation Y and the red one for Rotation X (Final Cut's and Motion's axis colours) clear without labels?
Should the 3D section show for every picked layer in a video, as now, or only once something has been turned?
Is View, Show Camera Settings an obvious enough way to the camera when the recording fills the whole frame and there is no empty canvas to click?
rough: The arcs only appear while the pointer rests on the knob, as decision card tilt-flip-and-push-layers-in-depth-from-the-canv-how-do-you-turn-a-layer-toward-o (option A, your call on 2026-10-11) describes; the mock's own editor frame draws them pinned. They then stay out while the pointer is anywhere over the layer, so the hand can reach the depth arrow.

On a still picture (a marked-up screenshot) the 3D section stays away until a layer has actually been turned with the arcs, so redlining keeps the panel it had; in a video it shows for every picked layer.

The 3D section sits under Effects rather than straight under Position and Size as the mock stacks it: Position and Size is no longer a panel section, and Color and Effects sit directly under Layers by your call on 2026-09-07.

The mock's thin Camera row at the top of the timeline for camera keys is not built, and in a video a click on the picture picks the recording rather than the frame, so the camera is reached by View, Show Camera Settings or the Canvas row: task show-the-camera-s-keys-on-a-thin-row-at-the-top.
The depth arrow's reading depends on the zoom (2.5 points of depth per screen point at 100%), so the same drag pushes further when zoomed out.
A walk photographs the window behind another app; the camera picture was taken with the app in front.
